confirmed: Source version is correct: arXiv:2608.30424v1 [cs.HC], 31 Aug 2026, 24 PDF pages, including Appendices A-D; the entire markdown was read (PDF p. 1, stamp; pp. 17-24, appendices; PDF page count).

Study 1 has 11 people and Study 2 has 10, 21 total; both are below 50. Each person completes both conditions, so arm counts must not be added as independent people (PDF p. 11, Sec. 5.1; p. 13, Sec. 5.4).

Random allocation is to Study 1 or Study 2; condition-order randomized counts and exclusions are not reported. Null arm-level randomized counts and assignment.randomized = not_stated are supported (PDF p. 11, Sec. 5.1; pp. 21-22, Appx. C.1-C.4).

Both arms in both studies use generative AI, supporting ai_design. The system uses Claude Sonnet 4, claude-sonnet-4-20250514-v1:0, up to three Functional Agents from 14 support types, and a 20-second inactivity threshold (PDF p. 10, Sec. 4.2 and Fig. 6; p. 11, Sec. 5.1).
Two stories per person, 20-25 minutes per story, approximately 90 minutes per session, and an instruction for around 400 characters are correctly recorded (PDF p. 11, Sec. 5.1; p. 24, Appx. C.8).

S1-O1 numbers match exactly: Expressiveness CSI p = 0.005, Holm p = 0.034, RBC = 0.924, CLES = 0.669; two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank. Figure 7 shows participant scores with box plots (PDF p. 22, Table 7; p. 12, Fig. 7).
S1-O2 numbers match exactly: Total Score CSI p = 0.083, Holm p = 0.498, RBC = 0.606, CLES = 0.678; two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank (PDF p. 22, Table 7).

S2-O1 numbers match: one-sided Wilcoxon W = 26, p = 0.031, Holm p = 0.094, r = 0.86; open rates 20.5% w/ Cog versus 7.4% w/o Cog; Tabs r = 0.51, with no significant Tabs or Panel difference. Suggestion conversion is not significant after Holm correction (PDF pp. 12-13, Sec. 5.3).

All numbers in one_line_finding match the source; the Study 2 rates are descriptive engagement measures and its corrected test is not significant (PDF p. 11, Sec. 5.1; pp. 12-13, Sec. 5.3; p. 22, Table 7).

No user-evaluation endpoint scores story creativity or diversity: measures are questionnaires and interaction-log engagement. The Scorer agent is a support feature, not a reported comparative evaluation outcome; core = no, criterion 3 = not_met, context_class = none, and has_randomized_people_study = false are supported (PDF p. 11, Evaluation Metrics; pp. 12-13, results; p. 22, Appx. C.3-C.4; p. 23, Appx. C.5).
The literature review develops a support-function taxonomy, with no pooled creativity estimates, intervals or standardizers; the synthesis fields can remain empty/null (PDF p. 6, Sec. 3.4).
summary: The reported numbers and exclusion from core/context evidence are supported: the two user studies have 11 and 10 people and no creativity or diversity outcome scored on their stories. Corrections are needed to both lab_rct labels, the omitted formative-study entry, the suggestion-conversion metric label, and the company-involvement field.
